lgtv:
A sleep timer that runs directly on an LG webOS television.
Stores the timer on the TV instead of keeping a phone or computer awake.
Offers preset durations, custom timers and cancellation from the TV interface.
Includes a Mac command-line client and a shared Swift control package.
Helps viewers end late-night watching without an always-on companion server.
Tested on one LG model; Developer Mode is required and the iOS app is planned.
v-home:
An ad-free LG webOS launcher with a shared household dashboard.
Organizes favorite apps, folders, HDMI inputs and wallpapers around remote navigation.
Adds household notes, plans, photos and a phone companion.
Integrates V/TV Sleep rather than creating a second shutdown scheduler.
Helps households reach their apps and shared information from one screen.
Requires Developer Mode; its optional Mac helper redirects LG Home on a best-effort basis.
di-GSTIN-Generator:
An invoicing and purchase-order workspace for Indian small businesses.
Reuses company, client and service records to reduce repeated data entry.
Supports GST tax splits, several document types and A4 PDF output.
Combines browser-local storage with optional Supabase authentication and sync.
Helps consultants and studios prepare consistent business documents with less manual work.
Built with Next.js and TypeScript; tax features require business-specific review.
di-form-engine:
A branded questionnaire portal for agency and client collaboration.
Brings written answers, uploads and voice responses into one project workspace.
Supports saved progress so clients can contribute across several sessions.
Its workflow build adds answer-level review, follow-ups and brief sign-off.
Helps studios turn scattered client inputs into clearer creative briefs.
Built with TypeScript; README distinguishes deployed features from pending workflow releases.
di-portal:
An administration portal for client-facing digital services.
Manages digital business cards, printed QR destinations and flipbook service records.
Tracks which services a client has, together with fees and renewals.
Lets printed codes point to updated destinations without reprinting.
Helps a small studio operate recurring digital services from one place.
Visitors use public links; message handoffs leave the actual send action to a person.
Innsaeit-client-dashboard:
A shared artwork pipeline tracker for a design studio and its clients.
Organizes production progress through a configurable staged workflow.
Separates client workspaces through tenant-aware data access.
Combines a React interface, Supabase data and Cloudflare R2 file storage.
Helps teams find project status and supporting artwork without scattered updates.
Designed so another client can be added through configuration rather than another build.
Chapter-members:
An administration workspace for business-networking chapters.
Tracks members, meetings, attendance, visitors and monthly dues.
Records meeting expenses and a running chapter treasury balance.
Includes role-based access, chapter separation and Excel import/export.
Helps volunteer leadership teams keep operational and financial records together.
Built with Next.js, TypeScript, PostgreSQL and Prisma.
hitechAC-Invoice-studio:
An HVAC business instance of the GST Invoice Studio platform.
Starts from a shared invoicing and purchase-order baseline.
Provides a configuration boundary for industry documents, branding and numbering.
Retains GST-oriented billing rather than starting a separate accounting system.
Targets less repetitive paperwork for an air-conditioning service business.
Repository docs separate inherited platform features from the ongoing HVAC instance build.
invoice-studio-Verax:
A separate repository using the GST Invoice Studio application baseline.
Supports invoices, purchase orders, saved clients and service catalogues.
Includes GST calculations, document previews and downloadable PDF output.
Uses local browser storage with optional Supabase cloud synchronization.
Helps small service businesses prepare repeatable documents without a full ERP.
Built with Next.js and TypeScript; independent Verax customization is not established by its README.
di-flipbook:
A publishing tool that turns PDFs and images into page-turning web links.
Processes uploaded pages in the admin browser before storing optimized images.
Serves branded viewers with publication status and expiry controls.
Supports client domains through a shared Next.js application.
Helps studios distribute brochures and catalogues as easy-to-open digital editions.
Built with TypeScript, Supabase and react-pageflip.
di-outreach-cockpit:
A single-user outreach CRM for a small creative studio.
Tracks prospects from initial research through conversations and booked calls.
Keeps contact details, research signals and activity history beside each lead.
Schedules follow-up tasks and drafts messages using configured language models.
Helps an independent studio keep warm opportunities from disappearing into notes.
Built around a focused Supabase and Vercel deployment.
Handshake:
A relationship-memory system for people who meet and maintain many contacts.
Imports conversations and proposes facts, promises and follow-up tasks with citations.
Keeps proposed interpretations separate from facts approved by the user.
Drafts replies and opens message links while leaving sending to a person.
Helps users remember context and meet commitments across their network.
Includes contact capture, review queues and integrations with personal knowledge tools.
handshake-os:
A next-generation relationship workspace built on the open-source Twenty CRM.
Packages a private relationship application with self-hosted infrastructure.
Ports relationship logic and tests from the earlier Handshake system.
Combines PostgreSQL, Redis and optional messaging and model services.
Targets more maintainable personal contact memory and follow-up workflows.
An ongoing rebase; the earlier system remains separate until an explicit cut-over.
career-ops-system:
A shared console with separate business-development and job-search workflows.
Collects opportunities and organizes them for review rather than mixing both pipelines.
Includes deduplication, scoring, drafting and scheduled processing stages.
Uses Next.js, Supabase PostgreSQL and configurable AI assistance.
Helps users review relevant opportunities and keep next actions in view.
Shared infrastructure does not mean shared outreach or automatic permission to contact people.
Career-console:
An empty repository reserved under the Career Console name.
No application code or default README was present at this review.
It currently provides no user-facing career workflow.
Its name alone does not establish features, architecture or integrations.
Any eventual benefit depends on a future specification and implementation.
Listed for completeness as a placeholder, not a finished portfolio application.
personal-brain-os:
A self-hosted capture and processing layer for an Obsidian vault.
Accepts notes, links, photos and audio into a reviewable filing pipeline.
Produces ordinary Markdown notes and surfaces extracted action items.
Adds a phone-friendly cockpit and relationship context around the vault.
Helps users turn scattered captures into searchable knowledge and practical next steps.
Uses Python, FastAPI, React and SQLite while keeping durable notes as portable files.
brain-vault:
A private backup repository reserved for the Brain OS Obsidian vault.
Its stated role is receiving vault backups from the cockpit pipeline.
Separates knowledge storage from the application's processing code.
The repository was empty when reviewed; no backup contents were inspected.
Its intended benefit is a recoverable, versioned home for personal Markdown notes.
Backup automation and successful recovery are not independently verified here.
brand-intelligence-os:
A local-first evidence collection and brand research system.
Crawls public websites and gathers available social and advertising evidence.
Preserves source outputs, screenshots and failed collection attempts.
Builds cited analysis packages for strategy reports assisted by Claude.
Helps brand strategists connect recommendations to inspectable source material.
Built with Python; unavailable evidence is kept distinct from claims that nothing exists.
ebooks-dashboard:
A private ebook dashboard for uploading and organizing EPUB and PDF files.
Converts books to Markdown and extracts covers for a searchable library.
Creates embeddings to support questions across the collection.
Uses a Next.js interface with a GitHub Actions processing pipeline.
Helps readers retrieve material without manually searching each book.
Stores library artifacts in a private repository and requires configured model providers.
prompt-database:
A reusable prompt-library project organized by categories and prompt types.
Its data layer supports storage, ranking, import/export and Markdown parsing.
Includes seed prompts and usage tracking for frequently reused material.
Separates state management from the planned browser interface.
Targets easier retrieval and maintenance of recurring creative prompts.
The README marks the data layer complete and the restructured UI still to build.
mcp-for-marketplace:
A distribution package for connecting FormEngine to Claude Code and Codex.
Contains plugin manifests, connector configuration and an MCP Registry entry.
Provides a questionnaire-writing skill and launch preparation material.
Its intended tools preview questionnaires and save authenticated studio drafts.
Helps teams bring questionnaire preparation into their existing AI work tools.
Not launched in the repository documentation; excludes sending, answer access and deletion.
private-markdown-converter:
A locally installed web app for converting common files into Markdown.
Handles documents, PDFs, spreadsheets, images and other supported inputs.
Offers optional advanced PDF processing and metadata-only conversion history.
Uses a macOS launcher around a local Python and Streamlit service.
Helps users prepare portable text for notes, search and downstream tools.
Current installation needs Python and dependencies; optional integrations need their own setup.
font-drop:
A macOS menu-bar utility that installs fonts from newly added ZIP files.
Watches a chosen folder and selects supported font files from incoming archives.
Prefers OTF where available and avoids overwriting existing installed fonts.
Handles nested archives, incomplete downloads and cloud-only file cases.
Helps designers spend less time unpacking and installing font families by hand.
Built with shell tooling and a small native wrapper; requires macOS setup prerequisites.
font-lab:
A browser workspace for comparing a supplied list of fonts on brand text.
Resolves installed fonts, dropped files and supported online font catalogues.
Provides comparison, wordmark and brand-proof views with per-font controls.
Exports visual proof sheets as PNG for design review.
Helps designers evaluate their chosen typefaces using the actual words they need.
Built with React and TypeScript; unavailable commercial fonts remain clearly identified.
sugoonj-patterns:
A browser-based drawing tool that turns frequency settings into visual marks.
Uses numerical models of vibrating plates and fluid-surface waves.
Offers multiple render styles for the same deterministic pattern.
Exports scalable SVG, high-resolution PNG and organized collections.
Helps a brand develop repeatable graphic assets from a consistent generative system.
Runs without a backend; frequency presets carry no health or wellbeing claims.
innsaeit-video-editor:
A local pipeline for turning raw vertical clips into branded short videos.
Uses an explicit edit plan through ingest, analysis, validation and rendering stages.
Supports formats for Instagram Reels and LinkedIn posts.
Offers Claude Code, local Ollama and deterministic editing directions as fallback options.
Helps creators repeat a branded editing workflow when model access changes.
Built with Node.js and FFmpeg; installation requires local media-processing tools.
innsaeit-wishes:
An interactive digital bouquet builder for personal greetings.
Lets users choose flowers, compose a card and change the arrangement.
Supports colorful and black-and-white presentation styles.
Creates shareable links and story images with a saved bouquet garden.
Helps people send a more personal visual message without physical delivery.
Built with React, SVG artwork and serverless link helpers.
font-installer-mac:
An early placeholder for a macOS font installation tool.
Its README explicitly directs users to the working Font Drop repository.
No installer implementation is provided in this repository.
Kept as a reference point for older links and project history.
The related user benefit is automated font installation through Font Drop.
Listed as superseded rather than presented as a second completed utility.
LOGO:
A scratch repository reserved for logo explorations and source artwork.
Its README proposes organizing concepts and final marks by brand.
Suggested assets include editable vector files and rendered previews.
No logo files were present according to the repository documentation.
The intended benefit is a clearer handoff between concept work and approved identity assets.
Currently a planning container, not a shipped design application.
money-view:
A mobile-first workspace for understanding personal cash flow.
Brings income, spending, budgets, statements and holdings into one interface.
Uses integer paise and India-time conventions for financial records.
Includes a guided question interface with confirmation before supported changes.
Helps users connect day-to-day transactions with a larger spending plan.
Built with Next.js and Supabase; financial totals are kept out of hosted question routing.
wealth-os:
An India-focused personal finance application built around statement imports.
Checks statement arithmetic before allowing parsed transactions into the database.
Provides review, categorization and financial dashboard workflows.
Tracks values in integer paise and avoids passing money values through language models.
Helps users build a more trustworthy picture of cash flow and holdings.
Built with Next.js and Supabase; repository verification covers its ingestion core.
storage-pilot:
A local macOS utility for storage audits and guided recovery.
Inventories selected folders and explains reclaimable space before actions.
Supports verified external project copies and journaled restore workflows.
Keeps destructive and cloud-managed operations behind explicit capability gates.
Helps users understand disk pressure while prioritizing recoverable data.
A Python prerelease; several GUI, restore and cloud milestones remain open.
sure_am_convertor:
A verification harness for preparing finance imports for Sure.
Contains paired sample inputs and expected transaction, trade and account CSVs.
Documents date formats, amount signs and category mapping expectations.
Uses synthetic fixtures to expose conversion errors before real data is imported.
Helps a future converter preserve financial meaning across different source formats.
The README describes test targets; it does not establish a finished converter application.
spend-ledger:
A repository named for the Spend Ledger personal-finance project.
Its default branch currently contains only a minimal README.
No expense-entry interface or processing implementation is present here.
Related finance work references a separate live ledger, which this repository does not document.
The intended area is keeping personal spending records easier to review.
Listed as a placeholder; working application capabilities cannot be inferred from its name.
keri-crafts-site:
A lightweight brand website for small-batch Gujarati pickles and preserves.
Presents current products, taste profiles, gifting options and ordering guidance.
Opens structured WhatsApp enquiries with product and quantity details.
Uses plain HTML and CSS without a cart or payment backend.
Helps customers explore a batch while keeping order handling personal for the maker.
Kept public temporarily to preserve its existing GitHub Pages hosting.
atarva-website:
A one-page website for an IT and design services business.
Uses Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS and motion components.
Includes a branded maintenance mode while website updates are underway.
Documents contact-form and booking-calendar integration points.
Helps prospective customers understand the business and find a contact route.
Kept public temporarily because GitHub Pages is enabled for this repository.
Avarta_brand_guidelines:
A configurable platform for delivering brand guidelines and assets.
Stores each brand's tokens, content and files in its own data folder.
Routes multiple brand domains through one shared deployment.
Includes brand-aware access and a studio overview of configured portals.
Helps teams find the correct identity assets and reuse consistent brand rules.
Build scripts turn structured brand data into repeatable client portals.
Design-innsaeit-Presentation:
An HTML presentation introducing a branding and packaging studio.
Explains services, working approach and selected visual case studies.
Uses browser-based slides with keyboard navigation.
Connects brand identity and packaging work to practical business conversations.
Helps prospective clients and referral partners understand the studio's offering.
A presentation artifact rather than an operations application.
Design-Innsaeit-pharma:
A browser-based presentation collection for health-brand outreach.
Contains a cold-outreach deck and a landing page for available presentations.
Explains a proposed research, positioning, design and delivery approach.
Organizes the studio's offering for nutraceutical and OTC business conversations.
Helps founders assess whether a brand-strategy engagement fits their needs.
Deck content is pitch material; market figures and case claims are not independently verified here.
hitech-deck:
A seven-slide HTML proposal for an operations-console engagement.
Frames current coordination problems and a proposed staged delivery plan.
Separates foundation, visibility and later roadmap scope.
Supports keyboard controls and browser-based presentation.
Helps a business compare a proposed operating system with its existing workflow.
A dependency-free pitch artifact; its roadmap is not a claim of shipped modules.
Innsaeit-os:
A personal launchpad for a studio's apps and administration consoles.
Collects app links, infrastructure dashboards and provider shortcuts.
Renders its entries from a single typed configuration file.
Points to credential-management pages without storing credentials itself.
Helps an operator spend less time finding the right service or dashboard.
Built as a small web interface focused on navigation rather than business-data storage.
DI-url-shortner:
A link-shortening repository based on the open-source Sink project.
Its documented foundation runs on Cloudflare infrastructure.
Provides short-link management and analytics capabilities from that foundation.
Uses the upstream Nuxt and Tailwind application stack.
Can help a studio share compact links and understand how they are used.
Upstream implementation is credited; project-specific changes are not established by the README.
Designinnsaeit-calendar:
A self-hosted scheduling repository based on Cal.diy, the Cal.com community edition.
Provides an upstream foundation for appointment booking and calendar workflows.
Targets personal control over scheduling infrastructure and configuration.
Can help reduce the back-and-forth involved in arranging a meeting.
The README recommends personal, non-production use and requires competent server administration.
Upstream authorship is credited; studio-specific customization is not established by the README.
sunshine-grove:
A personal daily wellness dashboard with meals, movement and habit tracking.
Combines editable vegetarian meal plans, recipes and shopping-list assistance.
Adds glucose logging, charts and a space for personal reflections.
Uses streaks and lightweight progress feedback to support daily routines.
Helps a household keep chosen plans and check-ins in one approachable interface.
Built with React; designed to support an existing care plan, not provide medical advice.
sunshine-meal-planner:
A household meal-planning progressive web application.
Uses a shared cloud data model with local read caches.
Supports household membership and separate admin, editor and member roles.
Includes authentication and configured image-upload infrastructure.
Targets less fragmented meal coordination across people in the same household.
Built with React, Vite, TypeScript and Supabase; setup requires household provisioning.
